title: DesiredGainR: DGSI and QGSI Workflows
text: DesiredGainR provides two distinct multi-trait selection indices. DGSI calibrates linear score towards breeder-defined desired responses. QGSI predicts quadratic economic merit genomic estimated breeding values (GEBVs). package infer genetic values, fit upstream genomic model, treat desired gains economic weights.
code: traits <- c("yield", "protein", "disease") n <- 60 candidates <- data.frame(   GenoID = paste0("G", seq_len(n)),   Family = rep(paste0("F", 1:6), each = 10),   yield = rnorm(n),   protein = rnorm(n),   disease = rnorm(n) ) G <- cov(candidates[traits]) dimnames(G) <- list(traits, traits)

title: DesiredGainR
text: DesiredGainR provides two auditable multi-trait selection-index engines plant breeding: run_dgsi() fits optimised Desired-Gain Selection Index (DGSI). run_qgsi() fits evaluates Quadratic Genomic Selection Index (QGSI) following Cerón-Rojas et al. (2026). methods answer different questions. DGSI searches linear index whose selected-set response approaches breeder-defined gains. QGSI predicts quadratic economic merit genomic estimated breeding values (GEBVs). Desired gains economic weights, DesiredGainR never substitutes DGSI desired-gain vector QGSI weights. DesiredGainR fit upstream multi-trait genetic model. Breeders provide genetic predictions, covariance information, breeding objective produced appropriate quantitative-genetic analysis. genuine genetic covariance matrix unavailable, estimate_genetic_covariance() provides explicit, labelled approximations.

Estimating total genetic covariance related candidates requires prediction-error covariance fitted multivariate model, including relevant relationship structure. BLUEs, adjusted phenotypic means, raw phenotypes contain residual environmental covariance. covariance identify genetic covariance without genetic model, replication, relationship information passed function genetic predictions.

title: Fit and evaluate a quadratic genomic selection index — run_qgsi
text: run_qgsi() implements quadratic genomic selection index (QGSI) $$I_{qg,} = w^\mathsf{T}\hat{\gamma}_i + \hat{\gamma}_i^\mathsf{T}W\hat{\gamma}_i,$$ \(\hat{\gamma}_i\) vector trait genomic estimated breeding values (GEBVs), \(w\) contains linear economic weights, \(W\) symmetric matrix economic weights squared cross-product genetic merit. Desired gains economic weights used construct either \(w\) \(W\).

title: DesiredGainR 0.3.0
text: Removed author-named DGSI wrapper; run_dgsi() now sole public desired-gain index entry point. Added estimate_genetic_covariance() clearly distinguished prediction covariance, PEV-corrected, SE-diagonal-corrected, relationship-adjusted estimators, together assumptions provenance. Implemented QGSI genomic covariance estimation reference GEBVs using Supplementary Equations 19.1 19.2 Cerón-Rojas et al. (2026). Added model-based QGSI mean, linear quadratic variance, normal-selection intensity, expected net-merit response, expected per-trait gains. Added optional simulation-squared accuracy mean squared prediction error calculations true genetic covariance matrix supplied. Added exact top-ranked selection clearly separated observed GEBV differentials expected realised genetic gain. Separated DGSI desired gains QGSI linear quadratic economic weights throughout combined pipeline. Removed unsupported constructor fabricated quadratic economic weights desired gains empirical correlations. Added equation-level tests scores, contributions, covariance estimators, response parameters, relationship-matrix alignment, selection.

title: DesiredGainR 0.2.0
text: Renamed package DGQGSI DesiredGainR. Added canonical run_dgsi() run_qgsi() interfaces. Required explicit genetic covariance matrix DGSI recorded provenance P G. Changed threshold selection eligibility followed index ranking. Added automatic best-replicate selection, convergence, coefficient, ranking selected-set stability diagnostics. Made missing-value handling explicit. Required explicit symmetric quadratic-weight matrix QGSI. Added candidate-specific linear, squared cross-product contributions.
